decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - 1.	The proposed development of five houses on the site is considered to be unacceptable as it has not been satisfactorily demonstrated that the standard of the access way is sufficient to service residential development of this scale. The proposed arrangements for pedestrians would be inadequate, and are likely to give rise to conditions prejudicial to the free flow of traffic on the public highway and access road and increase in danger for traffic and pedestrians, contrary to policies ENV-B 1.1 New Development, T.1.4 Car and Cycle Parking and Servicing Facilities for Developments, T.2.1 Pedestrian Access and T.4.3 Traffic Implications of New Development of the London Borough of Hounslow Unitary Development Plan 2003.

Condition : 2 - 2.	The proposed development of five houses, by reason of layout, design and materials, has not satisfactorily demonstrated that the proposal would preserve and enhance the character of the Thorney Hedge Road Conservation Area and would adversely impact on the outlook of surrounding properties. The scale of development is considered to be excessive for the site and would result in the development not being subordinate to the surroundings. The proposal has not satisfied policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development), ENV-B.2.2 (Conservation Areas), H.4.1 (Housing Standards and Guidelines) and the policies of Planning Policy Statement 5: Planning for the Historic Environment.
description: Demolition of existing single storey garages and erection of five three storey 4-bedroom detached houses.
